version.changelog: Add reviewer-gate preflight and pending-review safeguards.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.2.2

The skill is a legitimate utility designed to help developers package Chrome extensions and prepare them for release on GitHub and ClawHub. It includes a security-focused script (scan_publish_surface.py) that proactively scans for sensitive data like GitHub tokens, Google Client IDs, and local file paths to prevent accidental leaks. The code follows best practices, such as using subprocess.run with argument lists to avoid shell injection, and the instructions in SKILL.md are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of extension publishing and metadata management.

llm.summary: The skill's files, scripts, and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (packaging a Chrome extension, scanning tracked files, generating release metadata, and rendering publish commands); nothing requests unrelated credentials or installs arbitrary remote code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the bundled scripts and required tools: python3 is used to run included scripts, git/gh are used to inspect repository state and to render GitHub commands, and ClawHub is referenced for optional publishing. The requested binaries are proportionate to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to operate only on the repo path the user supplies and to run the included scripts. The scripts read repository files (manifest.json, tracked files), inspect git remotes, and generate outputs; they also detect token-like patterns for leakage checks. They do not transmit data to external endpoints or exfiltrate secrets; generated publish commands may invoke networked CLIs (gh, npx/clawhub) but those are only rendered, not executed by the skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only). All code is bundled as scripts; nothing downloads or extracts external archives during install. This is the lower-risk arrangement for a skill that runs local repo tooling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables are declared; the only optional env var is CWS_PUBLIC_SITE_BASE to set reviewer-facing URLs. The scan looks for token-shaped strings (e.g., ghp_, sk_) but only to report leak candidates — it does not request credentials. One minor mismatch: the metadata lists 'clawhub' as a required binary, but the scripts only render an npx-based ClawHub publish command (so a user may instead need npx or the clawhub package rather than a system 'clawhub' binary).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill does not request permanent elevated presence or attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It writes outputs to paths specified by the user and otherwise operates only within the provided repo root.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: package an extension, scan tracked files for obvious leak patterns, and generate GitHub/ClawHub release metadata and publish commands. Before using it: 1) run it only on the exact repo path you intend (it reads all tracked files); 2) review generated commands before executing them (they include git/gh and an npx clawhub publish step that will perform network actions); 3) verify you have the needed CLIs (python3, git, gh, and either npx+clawhub or a clawhub binary); 4) treat any findings from the leak scan as sensitive — the scanner flags token-shaped strings but does NOT transmit them anywhere; and 5) be cautious if a repo contains custom reviewer gate scripts (the tool will detect and suggest running them locally). Overall the skill is internally consistent and not requesting unrelated secrets or performing hidden network exfiltration.
